title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples

epigraph.quote: Every downstream fluorine molecule—whether it etches a solar wafer or cools an apartment—traces its lineage back to a single corrosive reaction between fluorspar and sulphuric acid.
epigraph.author: Fluorochemical Engineering Primer

web_blocks.html: Tanfac Industries operates an integrated inorganic fluorine chemicals facility in Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu [2][4]. The 60-acre site serves more than 400 customers across 10 to 12 countries [2][4]. Revenue from operations reached ₹711.07 crore in FY26 [6]. This represented a 27.67% increase from ₹556.98 crore in FY25 [6]. Trailing twelve-month sales through September 2026 reached ₹784 crore [6][20]. The company reports under a single chemical segment in statutory accounts [4]. However, its commercial business spans four active revenue lines and one under-construction vertical [4][10][12].

web_blocks.takeaway: Hydrofluoric acid and its direct derivatives—now bolstered by Solar-Grade DHF—generate ~85% of Tanfac's revenue, while captive 100,000 MTPA Sulphuric Acid underpins the core reaction.

web_blocks.html: 1. Anhydrous & Diluted Hydrofluoric Acid (AHF / HF): AHF is the foundational building block for fluorine chemistry. Tanfac manufactures AHF inside rotary kilns at Cuddalore [2][4]. The reaction combines acid-grade fluorspar with concentrated sulphuric acid and oleum [2][4]. This process releases hydrogen fluoride gas [2][4]. The gas is condensed into 99.9%+ pure anhydrous liquid [4]. Alternatively, it is absorbed into water for diluted 40%–70% grades [4]. In October 2024, Tanfac doubled AHF capacity from 14,850 MTPA to 29,700 MTPA [7][10]. That ~₹100 crore brownfield expansion reached ~95% utilization in FY26 [7][10]. AHF serves as both a merchant chemical and captive feedstock [4][10]. It feeds Solar DHF, Potassium Fluoride, and the future HFC-32 facility [10][12]. High kiln utilization is the primary driver of fixed-cost absorption at Cuddalore [4][10].

Concrete End-to-End Example (AHF): Consider an Indian agrochemical intermediate manufacturer synthesizing a fluorinated herbicide [2][3]. The buyer could be co-promoter Anupam Rasayan or a Gujarat-based formulator [2][3]. The customer cannot safely import bulk AHF in small batches [3]. AHF boils at 19.5°C and causes severe deep-tissue chemical burns on contact [3]. The customer therefore contracts with Tanfac for scheduled deliveries of 99.95% pure AHF [2][3]. Tanfac manufactures the acid at Cuddalore using imported fluorspar and captive acid [2][4]. It loads the product into specialized pressure-rated stainless-steel ISO tanks [4]. Dedicated hazardous-cargo transport carries the containers to the customer's plant [4]. Tanfac bills on formula-linked monthly or quarterly contracts tied to fluorspar and sulphur indices [4].

2. Solar-Grade Diluted Hydrofluoric Acid (DHF): Tanfac commissioned this product line in two separate phases [9][10]. It installed 5,000 TPA on an AHF basis in June 2025 [9]. A second 5,000 TPA followed in October 2025, reaching 20,000 MTPA diluted [9][10]. Tanfac thus became India's first and sole domestic producer of ultra-pure Solar-Grade DHF [9][10]. Industrial HF is commonly used for steel pickling and glass frosting [4]. By contrast, solar-grade DHF requires parts-per-billion purity control [9]. Contaminants like iron, sodium, copper, and nickel must stay near zero [9]. Trace metal ions diffuse into silicon wafers during etching and ruin photovoltaic conversion efficiency [9].

Concrete End-to-End Example (Solar-Grade DHF): In November 2025, Tanfac executed a 3.5-year commercial agreement [14]. The supply contract is worth approximately ₹732 crore excluding GST through FY2028–29 [14]. The partner is Vadodara-based Kredence Electronics Materials India Pvt Ltd [14]. Kredence supplies high-purity wet chemicals to domestic solar photovoltaic cell manufacturers under the PLI scheme [14]. Indian cell manufacturers previously imported ultra-pure DHF from China or East Asia [14]. Those shipments faced 4–6 week freight lead times, working-capital lockup, and contamination risks [14]. Tanfac now processes captive AHF through multi-stage sub-boiling distillation at Cuddalore [14]. The acid is diluted with ultra-pure deionized water inside fluoropolymer-lined systems [14]. Cleanroom technicians verify parts-per-billion purity using ICP-MS testing [14]. Tanfac delivers certified batches domestically to Kredence without requiring new capital expenditure [14].

3. Specialty Fluorides & Aluminium Fluoride (~15% of Revenue): Tanfac upgrades basic HF into solid and complexed fluorides [4][10]. These products include Potassium Fluoride (KF), Potassium Bifluoride (KHF2), and Boron Trifluoride (BF3) complexes [4][10]. The company also manufactures Aluminium Fluoride (AlF3) [4][10]. Together with surplus acid, these lines contribute roughly 15% of revenue [10]. Specialty fluorides involve lower tonnage than bulk HF [10]. However, they serve high-value pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and petrochemical applications [4][10]. Strict batch purity and moisture control generate superior unit realizations compared to commodity AlF3 [4][10].

Concrete End-to-End Examples (Specialty Fluorides & AlF3): Consider Potassium Fluoride applications [4]. A pharmaceutical manufacturer in Hyderabad requires a Halex reaction to synthesize a drug intermediate [4]. This process swaps a chlorine atom for fluorine on an aromatic ring [4]. Standard HF is too corrosive for glass-lined reactors [4]. The customer instead purchases anhydrous spray-dried KF from Tanfac [4]. Tanfac neutralizes HF with potassium carbonate and dries it to strict moisture limits [4]. In catalyst markets, petrochemical producers buy Tanfac's BF3-etherate or BF3-phenol complexes [4]. These compounds function as Lewis acid catalysts for hydrocarbon resins and fuel additives [4]. Finally, primary aluminium smelters in Odisha purchase dry AlF3 powder from Tanfac [4][5]. The powder lowers melting points and enhances electrical conductivity in molten cryolite cells [4][5]. Tanfac keeps AlF3 production volumes capped because margins remain lower than specialty fluorides [4][5].

4. Sulphuric Acid & Oleum: Tanfac operates a 100,000 MTPA Sulphuric Acid plant at Cuddalore [10]. The facility operated at ~101% capacity utilization in FY26 [10]. Roughly two-thirds of this acid is consumed captively inside the HF rotary kilns [4][10]. Tanfac sells surplus Sulphuric Acid and high-strength Oleum (H2SO4·SO3) to regional buyers across South India [4][10]. Burning elemental sulphur is an exothermic chemical process [4]. The acid plant generates byproduct high-pressure steam during operation [4]. This byproduct steam reduces external power purchases across the Cuddalore complex [4].

Concrete End-to-End Example (Sulphuric Acid / Oleum): A textile dye manufacturer in Tamil Nadu requires 20%–23% Oleum for sulphonation [4]. Hauling fuming acid from western India involves high freight costs and transport hazards [4]. The customer procures merchant Oleum directly from Tanfac in lined road tankers [4]. Deliveries take place within a 300-kilometer radius of Cuddalore [4]. This regional arrangement minimizes transportation expense on heavy acid [4]. Concurrently, it provides Tanfac with a reliable regional outlet for surplus production [4].

5. Pipeline Growth Leg — HFC-32 (R-32) Refrigerant Gas: Tanfac approved a ₹495 crore downstream chemical expansion in January 2026 [11][12]. The centerpiece is a 20,000 TPA HFC-32 plant at Cuddalore targeted for late Q3 FY27 [11][12][20]. HFC-32 is a lower-GWP refrigerant replacing R-410A in residential air conditioners [11][12]. The plant reacts captive AHF with methylene chloride [11][12]. This process captures downstream margins rather than relying solely on merchant acid sales [11][12]. However, the business will compete against established incumbents such as SRF and Gujarat Fluorochemicals [4][12]. It must also manage pricing competition from Chinese export suppliers [4][5].

Concrete End-to-End Example (HFC-32 Pipeline): Commissioning is scheduled for late FY27 [12][20]. Domestic air-conditioner OEMs and distributors in Chennai or Pune will source bulk ISO tanks of R-32 gas from Tanfac [12][20]. They will charge inverter split air-conditioner compressors with this refrigerant [12]. This domestic supply will replace imported Chinese R-32 and blended R-410A cylinders [12].

book_subsections.title: Inside the Cuddalore Chemistry Engine
paragraphs: If you and I walked onto Tanfac's sixty-acre Cuddalore complex, we would see why this business is harder to replicate than a typical batch-chemical blender. Everything starts with two bulk commodities: elemental sulphur and imported acid-grade fluorspar. Tanfac burns the sulphur in a 100,000-tonne-per-annum sulphuric acid plant that ran at 101 percent utilization in FY26. That reaction throws off intense heat and steam, which helps power the site, and yields concentrated sulphuric acid and oleum. Most of that acid never leaves the gate; it is piped directly into rotary kilns where it reacts with fluorspar to liberate hydrogen fluoride gas.

From that single reaction, Tanfac's ₹711 crore revenue machine splits into four active streams. Roughly 85 percent of sales come from Hydrofluoric Acid and its direct derivatives. In October 2024, management doubled base AHF capacity to 29,700 tonnes per annum and ran it at 95 percent utilization. Because AHF is both a merchant product and the captive feedstock for every downstream molecule Tanfac makes, keeping those rotary kilns humming at 95 percent is what absorbs the plant's heavy fixed depreciation.

Picture a real-world customer workflow for base AHF. An agrochemical intermediate manufacturer in Gujarat—perhaps co-promoter Anupam Rasayan or a third-party crop-protection formulator—needs to build a fluorinated herbicide molecule. It cannot safely make or store bulk AHF on-site because AHF boils at 19.5 degrees Celsius and causes severe, deep-tissue chemical burns on contact. So it signs a scheduled supply contract with Tanfac. Tanfac produces 99.95 percent pure liquid AHF continuously at Cuddalore, loads it into pressure-rated stainless-steel ISO tank containers, and dispatches it across India via dedicated hazardous-cargo tankers, billing on formula-linked contracts tied to fluorspar and sulphur prices.

book_subsections.title: Solar Wafers, Pharma Catalysts, and the Next Leg
paragraphs: The newest crown jewel inside that 85 percent bucket is Solar-Grade Diluted Hydrofluoric Acid. Across June and October 2025, Tanfac commissioned 10,000 tonnes per annum on an AHF basis—equal to 20,000 tonnes diluted—becoming India's only domestic manufacturer. Solar cell fabs need parts-per-billion purity because even a microscopic trace of iron, sodium, or copper diffuses into silicon wafers during wet-bench etching and ruins photovoltaic cell efficiency. Previously, Indian cell makers had to import ultra-pure DHF from China or East Asia with four-to-six-week shipping lead times and working-capital lockup. In November 2025, Vadodara-based Kredence Electronics Materials signed a ₹732 crore, three-and-a-half-year contract with Tanfac through FY29. Tanfac takes captive AHF, purifies it through sub-boiling distillation and ultra-pure water dilution in fluoropolymer-lined piping, verifies parts-per-billion specs in its cleanroom lab, and delivers certified batches domestically with zero extra capex.

The remaining 15 percent of revenue comes from specialty fluorides, legacy Aluminium Fluoride, and surplus sulphuric acid or oleum. Let us walk through each one. When a pharmaceutical API producer in Hyderabad needs to swap a chlorine atom for a fluorine atom on an aromatic ring—a Halex reaction—to make a modern drug intermediate, liquid HF is far too corrosive for its glass-lined reactors. Instead, it buys spray-dried anhydrous Potassium Fluoride from Tanfac, made by neutralizing HF with potassium carbonate. When a petrochemical refiner polymerizes synthetic resins or fuel additives, it buys Tanfac's Boron Trifluoride complexes as a Lewis acid catalyst. When a primary aluminium smelter in Odisha runs its molten cryolite pots, it buys dry Aluminium Fluoride from Tanfac as an electrolytic flux, though management keeps that commodity volume capped to protect margins. And when a regional Tamil Nadu dye or detergent maker needs a sulfonating agent, it buys Tanfac's surplus 20-to-23 percent oleum by lined road tanker within a 300-kilometer radius.

Finally, management is building a fifth leg: a 20,000-tonne HFC-32 refrigerant gas plant backed by ₹495 crore of capex, targeted for late Q3 FY27. By reacting captive AHF with methylene chloride, Tanfac wants to supply lower-global-warming-potential R-32 gas directly to India's booming room air-conditioning market. It is a logical next step on the chemical tree, though it also moves Tanfac from a protected domestic solar niche into a more competitive refrigerant arena.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Notice the strategic symmetry in Tanfac's product tree: Sulphuric Acid feeds AHF, AHF feeds Solar DHF and Potassium Fluoride, and AHF will soon feed HFC-32. Integration lowers unit cost when utilization is 95%, but it also concentrates operational risk inside one 60-acre Cuddalore fence.

book_paragraphs: Let us walk inside the Cuddalore factory gates together and trace what Tanfac actually makes, who buys it, and why a buyer cannot simply switch suppliers overnight. Roughly 85% of Tanfac's revenue comes from Hydrofluoric Acid—both Anhydrous HF (AHF) and Diluted HF (DHF)—while the remaining 15% comes from Specialty Fluorides such as Potassium Fluoride, Potassium Bifluoride, Boron Trifluoride complexes, and by-product Sulphuric Acid and Oleum. On paper, those sound like abstract periodic-table names. In practice, they sit at the heart of three demanding industrial supply chains.

Consider a domestic agrochemical or pharmaceutical intermediate producer in Gujarat—including co-promoter Anupam Rasayan itself—synthesizing fluorinated active ingredients. Fluorine atoms dramatically improve the metabolic stability and potency of modern crop-protection molecules and drugs. That customer cannot store six months of Anhydrous HF in a backyard warehouse; AHF is one of the most corrosive, tightly regulated hazardous chemicals in industrial chemistry, requiring specialized ISO tankers and strict Pesos and Pollution Control Board clearances. Tanfac manufactures AHF by reacting imported acid-grade fluorspar with in-house sulphuric acid in rotary kilns, purifies it through distillation, and delivers it via dedicated hazardous-cargo tankers under annual or quarterly formula contracts.

Now look at the newest jewel in Chapter 2: Solar-Grade Diluted Hydrofluoric Acid. Imagine a Tier-1 Indian solar PV cell manufacturer—like Kredence Electronics Materials, which signed a ₹732 crore, 3.5-year contract with Tanfac in November 2025—running wet-etching and wafer-cleaning baths for monocrystalline silicon cells. Even parts-per-billion metallic impurities in DHF ruin cell efficiency. Historically, Indian solar cell makers imported ultra-pure DHF from China or Taiwan with long shipping lead times and supply-chain vulnerability. By commissioning 10,000 TPA (AHF-basis) of Solar-Grade DHF in 2025, Tanfac gave domestic cell makers a reliable, local, pipeline-ready alternative.

Finally, examine the Specialty Fluorides line—Potassium Fluoride and Potassium Bifluoride. Here, Tanfac reacts its captive HF with potassium hydroxide or carbonate to serve niche metal-treatment, glass-etching, and fluorination-catalyst buyers. The volumes are smaller than bulk AHF, but the value-add per tonne is higher, helping cushion—though not eliminate—the cyclical swings of base acid realizations.

Let us examine why customers qualify a fluorine supplier slowly and rarely dual-source lightly. In electronics and solar wafer etching, a single batch of Diluted Hydrofluoric Acid contaminated with trace iron, sodium, or heavy metals can etch uneven micro-pits into silicon wafers, ruining an entire shift of cell production worth lakhs of rupees. That is why Kredence Electronics Materials committed to a ₹732 crore, 3.5-year supply agreement with Tanfac through FY29 rather than shopping spot cargoes every month.

At the same time, notice the difference between contracted volume and locked-in margin. Even in specialty fluorides like Potassium Fluoride, Potassium Bifluoride, and Boron Trifluoride complexes—which serve pharmaceutical fluorination and metal surface treatment—customers negotiate quarterly or semi-annual raw-material pass-through clauses. When fluorspar or sulphur prices jump abruptly within a quarter, the manufacturer absorbs the timing lag until the next reset window.

Notice how each of Tanfac's three product pillars carries a distinct customer contract rhythm. Base Anhydrous HF moves on quarterly or annual formula-linked B2B supply contracts with agrochemical and fluorochemical buyers. Solar-Grade DHF moves under multi-year qualification and offtake frameworks—exemplified by Kredence Electronics Materials—where purity and uninterrupted domestic logistics outweigh spot price haggling. Specialty Fluorides like Potassium Fluoride and Boron Trifluoride complexes sell in smaller drummed or specialized lots to pharma and catalyst buyers, commanding higher per-kilogram realizations but requiring strict batch consistency.

Pause for a moment on why captive Sulphuric Acid and Oleum production inside Cuddalore matters to every downstream customer. In chemical manufacturing, sulphuric acid is both a vital reactant for liberating HF from fluorspar and a source of exothermic process steam. By producing sulphuric acid on site rather than hauling it in tankers from third-party smelters, Tanfac lowers energy costs and insulates its rotary kilns from regional acid shortages—even though global sulphur price spikes still ripple through quarterly margins.
